title: refactor-terraform-storage-constructs-for-vpc-private-deploys
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Consolidate and refactor Terraform constructs used by Private/VPC deployments to provide a single opinionated storage module that provisions and controls EBS, EFS, and S3 artifacts with secure defaults. Goals: (1) enforce encryption-by-default with explicit KMS key wiring for cross-account deployments, (2) standardize snapshot lifecycle policies and optional cross-region replication for backups, (3) expose easily configurable EBS volume profiles (gp3/io2), EFS performance/mode, and S3 lifecycle tiers for archive, (4) include built-in health checks and operational alerts (CloudWatch metrics + Lambda remediation hooks), and (5) provide clear upgrade/migration paths for existing stacks and terraform provider bumps. This ticket delivers the module, Terratest suites, CI automation, migration scripts, and rollout guidance for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module tf-private-storage is published to internal registry with versioned releases
Default behavior enforces server-side encryption: S3 SSE-KMS with customer-managed CMK by default, EBS/EFS encrypted with same KMS key unless explicitly overridden
Snapshot lifecycle (retention, tags, cross-account replication opt-in) configurable with sane defaults (30d retention, encrypted snapshots)
Health-check Lambda and CloudWatch dashboard deployed as optional submodule; alerts fire on missing snapshots, low free space, or failing EFS mount targets
Upgrade path documented for existing stacks including state migration steps and provider version compatibility (aws provider 4.x -> 5.x/6.x guidance)
Terratest coverage >= 80% for happy-path create/destroy and for key failure modes (missing KMS key, insufficient IAM perms)
End-to-end rollout plan (canary accounts, monitoring runbook, rollback steps) peer-reviewed and approved by Security and Infra teams
comments: 2026-03-02: Initial spike completed. Identified two major constraints: cross-account KMS usage requires explicit grant flows; EFS replication API limits impact snapshot strategy. - Ava

2026-03-04: Architecture review with Security. Decided to default to customer-managed CMKs and require documentation for KMS grants; Security requested auto-rotation notes. Action: add KMS rotation guidance and CI check for key policy templates. - Liam

2026-03-06: Design trade-off: single monolithic module vs three small modules. We chose a meta-module pattern (tf-private-storage) that composes smaller ebs/efs/s3 modules so teams can depend on individual parts. This reduces blast radius for upgrades. - Liam

2026-03-08: PR opened with initial module scaffolding and Terratest harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/742 - include test matrix for terraform 1.5 and aws provider 5.x/6.x. - QA to run tests in sandbox account

2026-03-10: Security review requested. Added explicit outputs for created KMS key ARN and IAM policy snippets for cross-account snapshot access. Security asked for a demo of the KMS grant flow; scheduling demo for 2026-03-15. - Ava

2026-03-11: Observability: proposed a lightweight CloudWatch dashboard (free-tier friendly) and an optional Datadog integration. Ops suggested adding a synthetic check that mounts EFS every 6 hours to validate mount targets. Action: add Lambda synthetic mount submodule. - Priya (Ops)
migration_notes: Provide terraform import helper for legacy EBS volumes: scripts/migrate/import_ebs.sh
State migration pattern: move state to workspace-specific S3 backend before module swap; sample command sequence included in docs
When upgrading aws provider major versions, pin provider in root module and run a plan in a canary account to catch semantic changes (notably snapshot encryption flags)
Cross-account snapshot replication: require a pre-created replication role and KMS grants; include helper CloudFormation template to bootstrap grants for new accounts
test_plan: Unit: static checks (tflint, checkov) ran in PR pipeline
Integration: Terratest scenarios for create/destroy with KMS, snapshot lifecycle, and EFS mount synthetic checks
Chaos: simulate KMS deny and ensure module surfaces meaningful errors and recovery steps
Staging rollout: deploy module to two non-prod accounts, run 7-day retention smoke to validate snapshot creation and cleanup
Canary production: enable module for low-risk customer in Dedicated cluster with 72h monitoring window before wide rollout
